content:
ashley: Heads-up — onboarding report for orion-7b-ql8 shows a weird pattern: tail latency spikes + intermittent OOMs at high concurrency. Seen on dedicated and hosted canaries.

matt: I saw that on dashboards too. memory fragmentation histogram looks like repeated small free ops after longruns.

jamie: Repro steps? sequence lengths / batch sizes?

ashley: Repro is easy — long-context chat tests. Sequence ~2048 tokens, default `max_new_tokens=1024`, batching target 8 (continuous batching). Start concurrency ~40 qps. OOMs show when seq_len + max_new exceed expected.

ashley: Paste from logs: ```ERROR: alloc failed: 0x7f... attempted 12.3G, available 11.9G; kv_cache fragmented: 132 small free ranges```

jamie: That log screams KV cache fragmentation + our batching merging requests with long max_new_toks. For quantized ql8 we have bigger per-token overhead in some kernels.

sanjay: Also saw prefetching window set to 400ms; that stacks prefixes and makes larger combined memory working set. Maybe adaptive_window_ms needs to be smaller for orion-7b-ql8.

matt: Quick experiment results from my local run: lowered `max_new_tokens` to 256, and `adaptive_window_ms` from 400 -> 120. Concurrency 40 -> no OOM after 30m. Latency p95 rose 10ms but throughput stable.

ashley: Nice. Did you change KV prune settings?

matt: Yes, `kv_prune_threshold` from 0.25 -> 0.45 (aggressive prune keeps more contiguous free ranges). That reduced fragmentation in the trace.

jamie: Any quality regressions from lowering max_new_tokens? For typical chat flows we should be safe — most user prompts expect <512 reply. But need UX/SE check.

ashley: I ran automated eval with the standard chat-turn set — no measurable drop in Rouge/BLEU-style metrics for common prompts. But long-form summarization tests obviously truncated.

sanjay: Proposal: make model config override defaults for orion-7b-ql8: `default_max_new_tokens=256`, `adaptive_window_ms=150`, `kv_prune_threshold=0.45`. Canary rollout to 10% first. Add a fallback policy to upstream model variant (orion-7b-ql8-large) when we detect >3 OOMs / 5m.

jamie: +1. Also add an alert rule for fragmentation ratio and repeated small free ranges metric (new metric: mem.fragmented_ranges_count > 100 for 5m).

ashley: I'll prepare the config PR. Plan: canary 10% hosted, 10% dedicated pool, monitor for 24h. If stable, roll to 100% and update docs about max_new_tokens for that model.

matt: For bookkeeping — test matrix attached: batch sizes [4,8,12], max_new [256,512,1024], quant modes [ql8, ql4]. Only ql8 + 1024 hit OOMs. ql4 showed lower mem but worse token throughput.

ashley: tagging @deploy-bot to trigger canary once PR merged.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued — will deploy model-config canary to hosted/dedicated pools at 1799005600.

ashley: Thanks. Also adding a short note for support runbook: if customers need long-form generation, route to orion-7b-ql8-large or increase dedicated capacity with explicit reservation.

jamie: One more item: follow-up perf test to see if we can improve kernel selection heuristics to avoid the extra per-token overhead on ql8. Filed ticket MM-4122.

ashley: Cool. I'll open the PR and include test artifacts + logs.
